picks.title: Your AI agent's UI is mediocre—and here's how to fix it
picks.excerpt: Agent-built interfaces default to lifeless boxes because nothing in the loop enforces craft. The author wires a 'UI/UX Excellence Prover' MCP into the agent so spring physics, eight interaction states per component, and spatial hierarchy become checkable requirements instead of taste.
picks.rationale: Turns 'craft' into machine-checkable requirements via an MCP the agent must pass — the most directly copyable workflow change in the pool.

picks.title: I got tired of reverse-engineering design systems by hand, so I built a Chrome extension
picks.excerpt: Tired of manually reading DevTools to reconstruct another site's type ramp, palette and spacing scale, the author shipped a Chrome extension that extracts a live page's design tokens automatically. It turns competitive teardown into a one-click token dump.
picks.rationale: A shipped tool that collapses hours of DevTools archaeology into a one-click token dump — competitive teardown becomes a routine step.

picks.title: Adobe releases Photoshop 27.9.1
picks.excerpt: Photoshop 27.9.1 moves the Remove tool into the contextual task bar, adds inline prompt tips to Generate Image, and lets you push multiple layers straight to Firefly Boards. Small release, but it shows the AI tools migrating into the default toolbar path.
picks.rationale: A concrete shipped release where AI tools move out of side panels and into the default toolbar path — the daily-use surface designers actually touch.

picks.title: How Figma made copy + paste faster
picks.excerpt: Figma walks through the engineering behind making copy and paste dramatically faster — the least glamorous interaction in the tool and one of the most used. A reminder that perceived craft in a design tool is mostly latency work nobody announces.
picks.rationale: First-party look at how the most-used, least-discussed interaction gets its feel — perceived quality as latency work, not visual polish.

picks.title: Makera links CNC software, mobile control and project sharing
picks.excerpt: Makera Studio pulls CAM, simulation, guided setup and mobile machine control into one environment for its Carvera desktop CNC line, plus a shared project library. It collapses the gap between a CAD file and a cut part for small design shops.
picks.rationale: Collapses CAD file to cut part into one guided environment, putting subtractive fabrication inside a small studio's normal prototyping loop.
